AiSuccessResponse.description: Generic success acknowledgement for mutations that return no data.

error.description: The error message, ready to be shown to the caller.

AiErrorResponse.description: Error body — a single human-readable message.

AiReasoningLevel.description: Provider-neutral extended-thinking depth. `off` disables thinking where the model allows it.

AiChatToolPermissionMode.description: How a tool call the model makes is approved: ask every time, auto-approve opted-out tools, or allow all.

AiChatToolPrefsScope.description: Which disabled tool list a read or write addresses: the caller's own (`user`, what an absent value means) or the one an administrator keeps for everyone (`tenant`), which every user's reads fold in.

tools.description: Extra tools offered to the model for this request.

isReasoning.description: Legacy extended-thinking switch; stands for `medium`. `reasoningLevel` wins when both are set.

reasoningLevel.description: Depth of extended thinking for the round; providers clamp it to what the model accepts.

prompt.description: Override the action's baked-in system prompt (replace or append).

toolInstructions.description: Usage notes of the MCP servers the caller holds the connection to, keyed by server type; folded into the system prompt as advisory text.

contextRooms.description: Instructions rooms connected to the chat as context, each with the skills the round may use.

knowledgeRooms.description: Knowledge rooms connected to the chat; the knowledge search tool of the round is limited to them. Each `id` has to be a DocSpace room id.

knowledgeRoom.description: A single knowledge room, as an older client sends it. Read only when `knowledgeRooms` is absent; send `knowledgeRooms` instead.

folderContext.description: The folder connected to the chat as the round's context. It becomes the location the model is told the user works in, and the entry the round is attributed to.

entityId.description: The entry the round is attributed to. A hint, resolved against the caller's own access.

AiActionArgs.description: Per-request options of an AI round: extra tools, the depth of reasoning, a system prompt override and the rooms and folder connected as context.

name.description: Tool name as registered on the MCP server (e.g. `"web_search"`, `"insert_text"`).

description.description: Human-readable description shown to the AI model and in the tools list UI.
examples: Read the contents of a DocSpace folder.

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema describing the tool's input parameters.

enabled.description: Whether this tool is currently enabled. Disabled tools are hidden from the AI model.

serverType.description: The server or tool group the tool belongs to (an MCP server name or a host tool group ID): the key a disabled tool is stored under, so a tool sent in `actionArgs.tools` is still matched to its group.

requireApproval.description: Whether the tool asks for approval before it runs, under the `auto` tool permission mode: `false` runs it without asking; `true` or absent leaves it to the always-allow list and the tool's MCP annotations (see `annotations`). Under `ask` every call asks and under `allow` none does, whatever this says. Host tools default to `false`; MCP and custom-server tools leave it unset.

annotations.description: The MCP tool annotations as the server declared them in `tools/list`; never sent to the model. Under the `auto` tool permission mode a tool that cannot destroy anything runs without approval - one annotated `readOnlyHint: true`, or one with an explicit `destructiveHint: false`; a destructive tool, and one with no annotations (the protocol's default is destructive), keeps asking.

AiMCPItem.description: Descriptor for a tool exposed by an MCP server.

AiToolAnnotations.description: MCP tool annotations (`Tool.annotations` in the protocol). All hints are advisory and optional; the protocol's defaults are `readOnlyHint: false` and `destructiveHint: true`, which is why an unannotated tool is treated as one that may destroy state.

cloud.description: The account the room belongs to; `docspace` for a room of this portal.

skills.description: The skills of the room the round may use, as `GET api/2.0/ai/context/get-room-skills` lists them.

AiContextRoomRef.description: One Instructions room a round runs with as context: the account and room ID from `GET api/2.0/ai/context/get-context-folders`, plus the skills of the room the round may use.

id.description: The skill's ID, as `GET api/2.0/ai/context/get-room-skill` takes it.

name.description: The skill's name, from its frontmatter.

description.description: What the skill is for, from its frontmatter; empty when it declares none.
examples: How to review a supply contract.

AiRoomSkill.description: A skill of an Instructions room: the frontmatter of one Markdown skill file. `name` and `description` are what the model is shown; the body is read through `GET api/2.0/ai/context/get-room-skill`.

cloud.description: The account the room belongs to; `docspace` for a room of this portal.

id.description: The room ID; anything that is not a positive integer is ignored.

AiKnowledgeRoomRef.description: One Knowledge room a round searches: the account and room ID from `GET api/2.0/ai/context/get-knowledge-folders`.

cloud.description: The account the folder belongs to; `docspace` for a folder of this portal.

AiFolderContextRef.description: A folder connected as the round's context - any folder of the portal, not only a room - named by its account and ID.

AiActionType.description: The AI action a request or an assignment applies to. Each action has its own assignment slot; `Default` is the profile used when an action's own slot is empty.

id.description: Storage-assigned message id (absent on inbound drafts).

text.description: The text of a `text` or `reasoning` part.

parentId.description: Id of the part this one belongs to, on `text`, `reasoning`, `source` and `tool-call` parts. On a `reasoning` part the chat library keeps the provider's thinking signature here.

image.description: An `image` part's picture, as a URL (usually a `data:` URL). For an image the user attached, a JSON string `{ ref, title, kind: "image" }` naming the stored attachment instead.

mimeType.description: A `file` part's media type. For a file the user attached, a JSON string `{ ref, title, kind: "file", path, type }` naming the stored attachment instead - the chat library carries the reference here.

data.description: A `file` part's content; empty when the part references an attachment. (A `data` part would carry its payload here too, as any JSON value; neither the chat library nor this service writes one.)

filename.description: The file name of a `file` or `image` part.

name.description: An `image` part's display name, or a `data` part's name.

argsText.description: A `tool-call` part's arguments as the model streamed them, JSON text.

result.description: A `tool-call` part's result, once the tool has run.

isError.description: Whether a `tool-call` part's result is an error.

artifact.description: Extra data of a `tool-call` part. While the tool runs, the chat library keeps its progress here as `{ progress: [{ progress, total?, message? }] }`.

payload.description: What the tool asks the human for.

interrupt.description: A `tool-call` part's pending request for human input.

messages.description: Messages of a sub-agent run inside a `tool-call` part.

metadata.description: Provider-specific data of a `tool-call` part - for a Gemini call, `{ thoughtSignature }`, which has to be sent back with the call.

content.description: Message content: either plain text or a list of typed content parts. One part schema lists every field of every part kind of the `@assistant-ui/react` 0.11 `ThreadMessageLike` union (text, reasoning, source, image, file, audio, data, tool-call) plus what the chat library adds itself (`name` on an image part, `metadata` on a tool-call part), so a strict client can read any stored part; each field says which kinds carry it.

createdAt.description: Creation timestamp, ISO-8601 on the wire.

reason.description: Why the message is in that state: `tool-calls` or `interrupt` for `requires-action`; `stop` or `unknown` for `complete`; `cancelled`, `tool-calls`, `length`, `content-filter`, `other` or `error` for `incomplete`. An `incomplete` message the chat stored carries `cancelled` (the round was stopped) or `error`.

error.description: What failed, on an `incomplete` message whose `reason` is `error`.

metadata.description: Per-message metadata. The chat library writes `custom` (with the round's `contextEntityId`) and `steps` (token usage per provider request); `unstable_state`, `unstable_annotations`, `unstable_data` and `submittedFeedback` may appear as well. Read it as an open map.

attachments.description: Attachments linked to the message (`id`, `type`, `name`, `contentType`, `status`, `content`). Read them as open objects.

AiThreadMessageLike.description: A single chat message as it travels on the wire.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. One of a canonical set — `"auth"`, `"model_not_found"`, `"rate_limit"`, `"timeout"`, `"network"`, `"bad_request"`, `"server"`, `"not_found"`, `"insufficient_funds"`, `"aborted"`, `"unknown"` — or a provider-specific string when the SDK supplies one verbatim.

examples: The provider is rate limiting requests.

cause.description: Optional nested cause, normalized through the same helper.

AiChatErrorPayload.description: Why a round failed or stopped early, as the message status and the stream report it: a stable `code`, a message safe to show the user, and the cause when there is one.

threadId.description: Target thread; a new one is created (with an auto title) when omitted.

actionArgs.description: Per-request options of the round: extra tools, reasoning, a prompt override and the connected context.

entityId.description: Optional entity (room) scope for profile resolution.

contextEntityId.description: The folder or room the user is in. Tools run against it and the model is told it is the user's location; falls back to `entityId` when omitted.

profileId.description: Session-level profile override for this request only.

AiSendStreamBody.description: Shared body of the two streaming send endpoints (`sendWithStream` and its OpenAI-framed twin) — the `Chat` action is implied, so there is no `actionType`.

AiChatEvent.description: One event of a chat stream, told apart by `type`: `message-start`, `message-delta` and `message-end` frame the assistant reply, `message-incomplete` reports a provider error or an unfinished answer, `thread-title` carries a generated title, and `tool-call-pending` pauses the round until the call is approved (`POST api/2.0/ai/ai/approve-tool-call`) or denied (`POST api/2.0/ai/ai/deny-tool-call`).

type.description: Emitted once per `sendWithStream` call, immediately after the user message has been persisted by storage and before the assistant stream starts. Carries the storage-assigned `id` and `createdAt`. The UI uses it to render the user bubble — no client-side optimistic placeholder is needed, which keeps the runtime tree free of phantom nodes from index-fallback ids.

message.description: The message the event is about, in the state it has reached.

messageId.description: The storage identifier of that message.

idx.description: The zero-based position of the pending tool call within the message.

threadId.description: The thread the event belongs to.

autoAllow.description: The tool runs without asking the user, as the user's tool permission mode decides: under `ask` never - the always-allow list, `requireApproval` and the annotations are all ignored; under `auto` a tool on the always-allow list, one with `requireApproval: false`, or one annotated `readOnlyHint: true` or `destructiveHint: false`; under `allow` every tool.

serverExecuted.description: The tool is run by the service itself: the client must not run it, only ask for approval (unless `autoAllow`) and approve or deny the call - an approval needs no `result`.

profileId.description: The profile that generated the title, when one was used.

AiOpenAIStreamChunk.description: A chunk or the terminal error envelope emitted on a failed stream.

id.description: The completion identifier, stable across every chunk of one response.

created.description: When the completion started, in Unix seconds.

model.description: The model that produced the completion - the resolved profile's model.

choices.description: The choices carried by this chunk. This service emits exactly one.

AiOpenAIChatCompletionChunk.description: One `chat.completion.chunk` of an OpenAI-compatible streaming response. Only the fields this service can populate are emitted - an OpenAI client tolerates the rest as absent.

index.description: The zero-based position of the choice. This service emits a single choice, so always 0.

delta.description: What this chunk adds to the choice.

finish_reason.description: Why the completion stopped, or null while it is still streaming.

AiOpenAIChunkChoice.description: One choice of a streaming completion, carrying the part this chunk adds.

role.description: Sent on the first chunk only, always `assistant`.

content.description: The text this chunk appends. Null when the chunk carries no text.

tool_calls.description: The tool calls the model requested, emitted in place of text.

AiOpenAIChoiceDelta.description: The incremental part of one choice - what this chunk adds to the assistant message.

index.description: The zero-based position of the tool call within the message.

id.description: The tool call identifier, quoted back when its result is submitted.

type.description: Always `function` - the only tool kind the API defines.

function.description: The call itself: the function name and its JSON-encoded arguments.

AiOpenAIToolCallDelta.description: The incremental part of one tool call the model requested.

AiOpenAIFinishReason.description: Why a choice of an OpenAI-compatible streamed completion ended, as the OpenAI Chat Completions format spells it; null while the choice is still streaming.

error.description: The error that ended the stream: its message, type, code and the offending parameter.

AiOpenAIStreamError.description: OpenAI streaming error envelope. When the upstream request fails mid-stream the OpenAI API emits a single `data:` line carrying an `error` object (no `choices`), then closes the stream — the official SDK turns this into a thrown `APIError`. Mirrors that shape so a host exposing an OpenAI-compatible endpoint stays wire-compatible.

threadId.description: Thread the assistant message belongs to.

messageId.description: Storage id of the assistant message holding the tool call.

idx.description: Index of the tool-call content part inside `message.content`.

message.description: A copy of the assistant message as it was when the tool call surfaced. Optional and ignored: the round resumes from the stored message. Leave it out - a long conversation's copy can push the body past the size limit.

actionArgs.description: Per-request options of the round: extra tools, reasoning, a prompt override and the connected context.

entityId.description: Optional entity (room) scope for profile resolution.

contextEntityId.description: The folder or room the user is in. Tools run against it and the model is told it is the user's location; falls back to `entityId` when omitted.

profileId.description: Session-level profile override for this request only.

AiToolCallData.description: Identifies a pending tool call to resume — mirrors the library `ToolCallData` (its serializable fields).

profileId.description: The identifier of the resolved profile.

AiResolvedAssignment.description: Resolved profile for an action — both the storage row and its ID.

providerType.description: The provider type of the profile. `external` sends every request through a transport the embedding application supplies while parsing the answers with the provider named in `basedOn`.

basedOn.description:
Selects the response-format parser used by the `"external"` provider. Ignored for any other `providerType`.

Supported values are `"openai"`, `"anthropic"`, `"mistral"` and `"openrouter"`. Remaining values (`"genai"`, `"stabilityai"`, …) are accepted by the type but not yet implemented; passing one raises an error at request time.

baseUrl.description: Base URL of the provider API.

key.description: API key or token. Optional for local providers.

headers.description: Extra HTTP headers sent with every request to this provider. Merged into the SDK client's default headers; an explicit `Authorization` here wins over the one derived from `key`. Honoured by the OpenAI-family providers.

modelId.description: Selected model ID within this provider.

reasoning.description: Whether extended thinking is enabled for this profile's model.

reasoningSupport.description: What the model can do with extended thinking, as the provider's catalogue reported it when the profile was saved; the effort choices in the chat follow it. When absent, the abilities are taken from the model ID.

contextWindow.description: Size of the selected model's context window in tokens, as the provider's catalogue reported it at save time (see `Model.contextWindow`). The engine's history compaction measures the thread against it; when absent the id-based table answers, and when that has no row either, `CompactionOptions.defaultContextWindow`. Hosts persist it with the rest of the profile.

capabilities.description: Bitmask of capabilities supported by the selected model.

canUseTool.description: Result of the live tool-capability probe performed at create time and on changes to `modelId` / `providerType` / `baseUrl`. `undefined` means the probe has never run for this profile (legacy record).

useResponsesApi.description: Result of the live Responses-API probe (parallel to `canUseTool`). `true` means the model speaks `/v1/responses` and the OpenAI provider must route through `client.responses.create` — required for gpt-5+ reasoning models that reject `reasoning_effort` together with `tools` on `/v1/chat/completions`. Probed at create time and whenever `modelId` / `providerType` / `baseUrl` change. `undefined` means the probe never ran (legacy record) — readers treat that as `false`.

isCloudProvider.description: Whether this profile uses a cloud-hosted provider (e.g. ONLYOFFICE DocSpace).

useProxy.description: Whether the chat client sends this profile's provider requests through the portal's proxy instead of directly. Has no effect when no proxy is configured.

createdAt.description: Creation timestamp (ms since epoch). Used to sort the AI models list newest-first.

AiProfile.description: Complete AI provider + model configuration saved by the user. Profiles are the primary way users save and reuse provider configurations.

AiProviderType.description: Provider type identifier. Accepts all 17 built-in types with autocomplete, plus any custom `string` for dynamically registered providers.

AiBuiltinProviderType.description: The built-in AI provider types. `external` has no transport of its own: the requests go through a transport the embedding application supplies and are parsed with the provider named in `basedOn`.

thinks.description: Whether the model can think at all. False hides the whole control.

canDisable.description: Whether `"off"` really turns thinking off. False means the model thinks always and off only drops to its lowest depth (or leaves the default depth, where there is no knob).

depths.description: Depths the model distinguishes, lowest first. Empty when thinking is an on/off switch with no depth (or the model doesn't think). A level not listed is clamped to the nearest one — see `clampReasoningLevel`.

defaultDepth.description: The depth the model runs at when nothing asks for one — what a stored `"off"` means on a model that cannot be switched off. Known only where a catalogue reports it (OpenRouter's `default_effort`); otherwise `DEFAULT_REASONING_LEVEL` clamped to `depths` is assumed.

AiReasoningSupport.description: What one model can do with extended thinking. Providers describe each model through this shape so the UI offers only the choices that change the request, and the request builders clamp to the same table.

AiReasoningDepth.description: A `ReasoningLevel` above off — a depth the model can think at.

AiAssignmentMutationResult.description: The outcome of an assign or unassign: a success, or an error naming the field that was refused.

success.description: True when the assignment was persisted.

error.description: Why the assignment was rejected. Present on failure.

message.description: The human-readable reason the field was rejected.

code.description: Optional: producers that know the reason set it (the prompts engine does).

AiErrorData.description: A field-scoped validation error: which form field was rejected, and why.

AiErrorCode.description:
Why a field-scoped operation was refused, independent of the wording of `message`, so a host can pick an HTTP status without parsing text:

- `"required"` — the field is empty.
- `"conflict"` — the value collides with an existing entry.
- `"not_found"` — the referenced entry does not exist.
- `"invalid"` — the value has the wrong shape or an unsupported value.

AiBulkAssignmentResult.description: The outcome of a bulk assign: either every entry was stored, or none was and the errors are reported per action. Every entry is validated before anything is written, so one bad entry never leaves the assignments half-written.

success.description: True when every entry was persisted.

errors.description: What was rejected, per action. Present on failure - and then no entry was persisted.

AiAssignmentsMap.description: Every action-to-profile binding of the scope: the action type is the key, the bound profile's id the value. An action with no binding is absent.

assignments.description: The bound profiles keyed by action type, as `GET api/2.0/ai/profiles/list` describes them. A binding whose profile no longer exists is left out.

profilesTotal.description: How many profiles the portal has.

chatProfilesTotal.description: How many of those profiles can chat; a profile without declared capabilities counts as one that can.

AiAssignmentsExpanded.description: The bindings with `expand=profile`: the bound profiles themselves, plus how many profiles the portal has, so a chat can start on this one read.

source.description: Where the attachment came from: `user` - attached by the user (also when unset); `tool` - produced by a tool call (for example `generate_image`).

examples: This agreement is made on 1 January 2026 between …

messageId.description: Owning message id once linked. Unset while the attachment is a draft.

threadId.description: Owning thread id once linked. Unset while the attachment is a draft.

entityId.description: The room or folder the attachment was created in, as an opaque token; once the attachment is bound to a message it repeats the thread's own scope.

canAnalyze.description: Whether the attached form can be analyzed.

formKeys.description: Keys of the fields inside the form. `key` is the field identifier, `text` its human-readable label.

AiAttachment.description: Persistent record for a single attachment (file or image) referenced from a user message. Files carry extracted text in `content`; images carry base64 data in `base64`. Metadata (`title`, `path`, `type`) is always present for display purposes regardless of whether the heavy payload is loaded.

question.description: The question as it is shown to the user.
examples: Which region had the most responses?

prompt.description: The prompt sent to the chat when the user picks the question.
examples: Group the submissions by region and show the count for each.

AiSuggestedQuestion.description: A starter question proposed for an attached form.

status.description: `ready` - the questions are there; `pending` - they are being generated and arrive over the socket, ask again later; `unavailable` - the attachment is not a form that can have any.

AiSuggestedQuestionsResult.description: The starter questions of an attached form, and whether they are ready.

cloud.description: The account the rooms belong to; `docspace` for this portal.

rooms.description: The rooms of that account the caller can connect.

AiContextFolder.description: The rooms of one account the caller can connect as context, grouped under the account.

AiContextRoom.description: A room the caller can connect to a chat as context.

The engine's history compaction measures the thread against it; when absent the id-based table answers, and when that has no row either, `CompactionOptions.defaultContextWindow`. capabilities.description: Bitmask of capabilities supported by the selected model.

canUseTool.description: Result of the live tool-capability probe performed at create time and on changes to `modelId` / `providerType` / `baseUrl`. `undefined` means the probe has never run for this profile (legacy record).

useResponsesApi.description: Result of the live Responses-API probe (parallel to `canUseTool`). `true` means the model speaks `/v1/responses` and the OpenAI provider must route through `client.responses.create` — required for gpt-5+ reasoning models that reject `reasoning_effort` together with `tools` on `/v1/chat/completions`. Probed at create time and whenever `modelId` / `providerType` / `baseUrl` change. `undefined` means the probe never ran (legacy record) — readers treat that as `false`.

useProxy.description: Whether the chat client sends this profile's provider requests through the portal's proxy instead of directly. Has no effect when no proxy is configured.

AiCreateProfileInput.description: Input for creating a new profile: the shape of a profile without the fields the service fills in (`id`, `createdAt`).

AiProfileMutationResult.description: Outcome of `create` / `update` — either a success carrying the persisted profile, or a failure with a field-level error description from the name check or the provider credential check.

success.description: True when the profile was persisted.

profile.description: The persisted profile. Present on success.

error.description: Why the profile was rejected - the name check or the provider credential check. Present on failure.

id.description: Model identifier as used by the provider API (e.g. `"gpt-4o"`, `"claude-sonnet-4-20250514"`).

name.description: Human-readable model name for display in the UI.

reasoning.description: Whether this model supports extended thinking / chain-of-thought reasoning.

reasoningSupport.description: What the model can do with extended thinking, when the provider's catalogue reports it (OpenRouter and the ONLYOFFICE route do). Copied onto the profile when it is saved; when absent, the abilities are taken from the model ID.

capabilities.description: Bitmask of model capabilities (Chat, Image, Vision, Tools, etc.). Used to filter models per `ActionType`.

contextWindow.description: Size of the model's context window in tokens, when the provider's catalogue reports one (OpenRouter and the ONLYOFFICE route carry `context_length`). Copied onto the profile at save time; absent, the widget falls back to the id-based table in `core/providers/context-window`.

created.description: Release date as a Unix timestamp in **seconds**, when the provider's catalogue reports one (OpenAI-shaped `/models` responses and OpenRouter carry `created`; Anthropic carries an ISO `created_at`). The model picker sorts on it so the newest releases come first; entries without it fall back to alphabetical order.

AiModel.description: AI model metadata. Describes a single model available from a provider.

id.description: Model revision id the key is set for, used in the path when replacing or deleting it.

name.description: Model display name; absent when the model is no longer in the gateway catalogue.

provider.description: BYOK provider id the key belongs to, e.g. `anthropic`.

id.description: BYOK provider id, passed as `provider` when setting a BYOK key.

image.description: SVG markup of the logo of the provider's models' owner.

models.description: Models that can be called through this provider with the portal's own key.

id.description: Model id, used in the path when setting its BYOK key.

provider.description: BYOK provider id from the model's `byok_providers`, e.g. `anthropic`.

examples: Summarise the key obligations and dates in the attached contract.

folderId.description: The folder to file the prompt under. Omit or send null to leave it outside any folder.

AiCreatePromptInput.description: Input for creating a prompt; the service fills in `id`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`.

AiPromptMutationResult.description: Outcome of `create` / `update` / `move` on a prompt — either the persisted prompt or a field-scoped error.

success.description: True when the prompt was persisted.

prompt.description: The persisted prompt. Present on success.

error.description: Why the prompt was rejected. Present on failure.

name.description: Prompt display name shown in the prompt picker.

text.description: Prompt template text. May contain placeholder tokens.
examples: Summarise the key obligations and dates in the attached contract.

folderId.description: Optional parent folder ID. `undefined` means the prompt is at the root level.

createdAt.description: Timestamp (ms since epoch) when the prompt was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp (ms since epoch) of the last prompt modification.

AiPrompt.description: Saved prompt template that users can quickly insert into the chat.

AiFolderMutationResult.description: Outcome of `createFolder` / `renameFolder` — either the persisted folder or a field-scoped error.

success.description: True when the folder was persisted.

folder.description: The persisted folder. Present on success.

error.description: Why the folder was rejected. Present on failure.

createdAt.description: Timestamp (ms since epoch) when the folder was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp (ms since epoch) of the last folder modification.

version.description: The bundle format version, so an import can migrate an older export.

AiPromptBundle.description: Versioned, self-contained bundle of every saved prompt and folder. Stable wire format — `version` lets the import path migrate older shapes if the schema ever changes.

AiImportMode.description: How an imported prompt bundle meets the library: `merge` adds to it, `replace` replaces it.

AiImportResult.description: The outcome of a prompt bundle import: either every entry was stored, with counts, or none was and the errors are reported per entry.

success.description: True when the whole bundle was imported.

imported.description: How many folders and prompts were created. Present on success.

errors.description: What was rejected, per entry. Present on failure - and then nothing was imported.

kind.description: `"folder"` or `"prompt"`, plus the offending name or id.

ref.description: The offending entry - its name or its id.

examples: a prompt of that name already exists

AiImportError.description: One refused entry of a prompt bundle import.

title.description: Optional thread title. Auto-generated from the first message if not set.

lastEditDate.description: Timestamp (ms since epoch) of the last message in this thread. Used for sorting.

provider.description: Provider configuration at the time of last message. Used for thread-level provider display.

AiMcpServerConfig.description: One MCP server configuration. The shape is intentionally open — MCP allows per-transport fields (`command`/`args` for stdio, `url` for HTTP, plus env, headers, etc.) and the storage layer stays agnostic to which transport is in use.

AiToolsMutationResult.description: Outcome of an MCP-server CRUD call. Either success or a field-scoped error suitable for the settings form.

success.description: True when the MCP server was persisted.

error.description: Why the MCP server was rejected. Present on failure.

AiToolsBulkResult.description: The outcome of replacing the custom MCP servers: either every entry was stored, or none was and the errors are reported per server.

success.description: True when every custom MCP server was persisted.

errors.description: What was rejected, per server. Present on failure - and then no server was persisted.

key.description: API key for the provider. Optional for self-hosted or keyless setups.

baseUrl.description: Optional override for the provider's base URL.

isCloudProvider.description: Whether this provider is cloud-hosted (vs. self-hosted).

headers.description: Extra HTTP headers sent with each request to the ONLYOFFICE / cloud backend (e.g. `X-Tenant`). Merged after the derived `Authorization` header, so a custom header of the same name wins.

AiWebSearchConfig.description: Web-search provider configuration. Credentials and provider selection for the built-in web-search tool group.

AiWebSearchMutationResult.description: The outcome of storing a web-search configuration: the stored configuration, or an error naming the field that was refused.

success.description: True when the configuration was persisted.

config.description: The persisted web-search configuration. Present on success.

error.description: Why the configuration was rejected. Present on failure.

dateValue.description: ISO 8601 date-time, UTC midnight of the date.

messageId.description: The user message to re-roll from: everything stored after it is deleted. When omitted, or no longer in the thread, the last user message is used.

keepCount.description: How many messages from the start of the thread to keep, used when `messageId` does not resolve. The message at `keepCount - 1` has to be a user message; otherwise the value is ignored.

expectedLength.description: The thread length the caller saw when it computed `keepCount`. When it differs from the stored length, `keepCount` is discarded and the last user message is used instead.

value.description: New extended-thinking depth; `off` turns deep mode off.

providerType.description: The provider type of the profile. `external` sends every request through a transport the embedding application supplies while parsing the answers with the provider named in `basedOn`.

basedOn.description:
Selects the response-format parser used by the `"external"` provider. Ignored for any other `providerType`.

Supported values are `"openai"`, `"anthropic"`, `"mistral"` and `"openrouter"`. Remaining values (`"genai"`, `"stabilityai"`, …) are accepted by the type but not yet implemented; passing one raises an error at request time.

baseUrl.description: Base URL of the provider API.

modelId.description: Selected model ID within this provider.

reasoning.description: Whether extended thinking is enabled for this profile's model.

reasoningSupport.description: What the model can do with extended thinking, as the provider's catalogue reported it when the profile was saved; the effort choices in the chat follow it. When absent, the abilities are taken from the model ID.

contextWindow.description: Size of the selected model's context window in tokens, as the provider's catalogue reported it at save time (see `Model.contextWindow`). The engine's history compaction measures the thread against it; when absent the id-based table answers, and when that has no row either, `CompactionOptions.defaultContextWindow`. Hosts persist it with the rest of the profile.

capabilities.description: Bitmask of capabilities supported by the selected model.

canUseTool.description: Result of the live tool-capability probe performed at create time and on changes to `modelId` / `providerType` / `baseUrl`. `undefined` means the probe has never run for this profile (legacy record).

useResponsesApi.description: Result of the live Responses-API probe (parallel to `canUseTool`). `true` means the model speaks `/v1/responses` and the OpenAI provider must route through `client.responses.create` — required for gpt-5+ reasoning models that reject `reasoning_effort` together with `tools` on `/v1/chat/completions`. Probed at create time and whenever `modelId` / `providerType` / `baseUrl` change. `undefined` means the probe never ran (legacy record) — readers treat that as `false`.

isCloudProvider.description: Whether this profile uses a cloud-hosted provider (e.g. ONLYOFFICE DocSpace).

useProxy.description: Whether the chat client sends this profile's provider requests through the portal's proxy instead of directly. Has no effect when no proxy is configured.

createdAt.description: Creation timestamp (ms since epoch). Used to sort the AI models list newest-first.

folderId.description: Target folder id, or `null` for root.

profile.description: Profile the title generation runs on.

firstMessage.description: First user message a fresh thread derives its title from.

entityId.description: Opaque scope token persisted on a freshly created thread.

entityMeta.description: Optional entity hint (lib 0.5.64): only `entityId` is read; the source (`source_id` / `source_type` / `source_title`) is re-resolved server-side before reaching the provider as metadata.

messageId.description: The stored message itself - with its storage-assigned `id` and `createdAt` - despite the field name, which is kept for the clients that already read it. The message ID is `messageId.id`.

prompt.description: What kind of metadata fields the caller is interested in; a hint for the model.

destId.description: The integer id of the Instructions room the skill is written for.

description.description: What the skill should do, at most 2000 characters; a specification for the model.

name.description: The skill's name as written in the frontmatter; the file is saved as `<name>.md`.

content.description: The whole Markdown file, frontmatter included. Nothing is saved.

Whether the values were only proposed (`true`) or written as well.
